articles.title: The International Pipeline Edge
articles.subtitle: Why some organizations consistently extract better ERA outcomes from acquired pitchers — and what the roster data says about why
articles.summary: Across FIP, xFIP, and SIERA — three independent ERA-family metrics — organizations with higher shares of international-born pitchers extract systematically better outcomes from acquired starters. The effect holds across 632 trade-pitcher observations from 2010–2024.

articles.title: Breadth Over Depth: The Award Pedigree Paradox
articles.subtitle: Getting several decorated players outperforms getting one star — and the data is unambiguous about it
articles.summary: A counterintuitive finding from Bayesian regression across 5,000+ trade legs: the share of acquired players with any award history predicts better outcomes, but the average award prestige per player predicts worse outcomes. Breadth is rewarded. Depth is penalized.

articles.title: The K% Mirage That Isn't
articles.subtitle: Pitchers on a strikeout spike regress on K% post-trade — but their ERA metrics hold. You're not buying a mirage.
articles.summary: The conventional wisdom is right that K% regresses after a spike — but wrong about what it means. The same pitchers post better FIP, xFIP, and SIERA outcomes. The strikeout rate was the ceiling; the pitch development was the floor.
